CFML Language Reference: Functions

IsDefined

Takes the name of a variable as a string and returns YES if it exists. The name may include a scope prefix (Form.Email, Session.CartID) and dotted structure keys (Customer.Address).

Category

Decision functions

Syntax

IsDefined("variable_name")

Parameters

variable_name
A string holding the variable name, in quotes. Do not wrap it in pound signs unless you want the value of another variable to be used as the name.

Returns

YES or NO.

Usage

IsDefined is the 4.x replacement for ParameterExists. Without a scope prefix it searches the scopes in the usual order (query columns inside a CFOUTPUT or CFLOOP over a query, then Variables, CGI, URL, Form, Cookie, Client). Use a prefix whenever you can: it is faster and avoids surprises.

Do not use IsDefined on array elements such as "Cart[3]"; KoldFusion happens to allow it, but portable code compares the index with ArrayLen instead. To give a variable a default value when it does not exist, CFPARAM is shorter than an IsDefined test.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Customer = StructNew()>
<CFSET Customer.Name = "Pat">
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Expression</TH><TH>Result</TH></TR>
<CFLOOP INDEX="v" LIST="Customer,Customer.Name,Customer.Email,Variables.Customer,URL.Color,Color,Form.Color">
<CFOUTPUT><TR><TD><TT>IsDefined("#v#")</TT></TD><TD>#IsDefined(v)#</TD></TR></CFOUTPUT>
</CFLOOP>
</TABLE>
<CFIF IsDefined("URL.Color")>
  <CFOUTPUT><P>Your favorite color is #URL.Color#.</CFOUTPUT>
<CFELSE>
  <P>Try adding <TT>?Color=Blue</TT> to the URL.
</CFIF>
